terms.definition: The force that pulls any two masses toward each other.
terms.whyItMatters: It holds moons, planets, and the whole solar system together, and gives everything its weight.
terms.whereItIs: Everywhere — pictured as inward arrows around the planet.

terms.definition: How strong gravity is at a location — about 9.8 m/s² on Earth.
terms.whyItMatters: Multiply it by mass and you get weight (W = mg); it is the 'g' behind every weighing.
terms.whereItIs: Tagged on the planet as 9.8 m/s².

terms.definition: Falling under gravity alone with no air resistance acting.
terms.whyItMatters: In free fall every object accelerates equally — the bowling ball and the feather land together.
terms.whereItIs: The vacuum tube that removes the air.

terms.definition: The looping path of an object that keeps falling around a body without landing.
terms.whyItMatters: Explains why the Moon, satellites, and planets all circle instead of flying straight.
terms.whereItIs: The dashed ring carrying the satellite.
